advice.advice: The prior attempt deleted the file inside task_func, but tests inspect it after return; deletion belongs to test teardown. Do not call os.remove or os.rmdir. Create task_func_data with os.makedirs(exist_ok=True), open 'task_func_data/Output.txt' in append mode, and write the header only if the file is new/empty (check os.path.getsize or existence before opening) so repeated calls don't duplicate headers. Append random temperature and humidity rows (with a timestamp column is fine). Return exactly the string 'task_func_data/Output.txt' (os.path.join yields the same on POSIX). Leave the file on disk after returning. Verify by calling twice and confirming one header and growing rows.

Your merge logic was right, but the totals were wrong: you summed the whole file after merging, so pre-existing rows were counted again. The expected Counter reflects only the *incremental* totals — the sum of the goals/penalties values you were given (e.g. empty/zero inputs -> Counter({'goals':0,'penalties':0}); a second call with the same dicts should not double-count prior file contents). So compute totals from the input mappings themselves (sum of goals.values(), sum of penalties.values()), while still merging into the CSV per-team rows and preserving the header. Also handle negative values (penalties can go negative) and missing files without crashing. Keep returning a Counter with keys 'goals' and 'penalties'.

The prior fix still reduced the wrong axis. Required: product shape (P.shape[0], T.shape[1], T.shape[2]) — contract P's last axis with T's first axis only, no extra .sum(). Use np.tensordot(P, T, axes=([1],[0])) and flatten with .reshape(-1,1); do NOT sum the trailing axis. Verify flattened length == P.shape[0]*T.shape[1]*T.shape[2] (e.g. 12 for the failing case, not 36 or 6). The duplicate-point ConvergenceWarning came from collapsing values; keeping the full tensor product yields distinct points so KMeans returns n_clusters labels. Return fit_predict output (labels array) and ax with exact title 'KMeans Clustering Visualization'. Sanity-check with small random arrays that len(cluster_result)==flattened.shape[0] and unique labels count is reasonable.
